ACME Ops: Hey team — since last night our inference p95/p99 for the `long-context-x2` model jumped ~3-4x. Users complaining about timeouts. We only started sending >8k tokens in a few flows; not sure if that's the trigger.
Maya (Support): Sorry you're hitting this, @ACME Ops. Can you paste a minimal request that reproduces it? Also where are you calling the hosted API from (region)?
ACME Ops: curl example below. We're hitting us-west-2. Repro is easy: send a 12k-token prompt (system + user chunks).
ACME Ops: ```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME...' \ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
  -d '{"model":"long-context-x2","input":"<12k tokens here>","max_tokens":2048}'
```
Tony (Eng Runtime): tagging in. @Li @Sara can you grab the trace id for one of the slow requests from our observability link? ACME, do you have request ids?
ACME Ops: I can grab one — request id `req_20260315_acme_47`.
Maya (Support): Thanks — forwarding to runtime. We also saw a small spike in errors around 03:12 UTC but it looks like latency is the main issue.
Li (SRE): Pulling traces: https://observability.redwood/trace/req_20260315_acme_47 — I'm seeing a large tail in tokenizer step (~70% of total). Tokenization for this model seems to be single-threaded and scaling linearly with input bytes.
Tony (Eng Runtime): Interesting. Long-context-x2 was onboarded with a new tokenizer binding last week (fast-tokenize-v2) to support extended vocab mapping. We tested with synthetic sequences but maybe not with many multibyte segments.
Sara (ML Ops): I see an increase in `tokenize_ms` for inputs with many unicode sequences and delimiter patterns — the fallback path from fast-tokenize-v2 to python-tokenizer actually triggers for certain rare token patterns and is expensive.
Maya (Support): Ok, short-term mitigation suggestions? We need something ACME can apply now.
Tony (Eng Runtime): Short term: 1) pin to `long-context-x1` (older variant) which uses the previous tokenizer (no behavior change in outputs for most apps), or 2) set `tokenize_mode: legacy` client-side to force the older tokenizer (we added this toggle for onboarding). Both are non-destructive.
ACME Ops: How do we pin to x1? Our code uses model alias `long-context`.
Tony (Eng Runtime): Use model parameter `model: "long-context:x1-stable"` in your payload. Example: `"model":"long-context:x1-stable"`. That will route to the variant with the previous tokenizer/kernels.
ACME Ops: Doing that now... testing.
deploy-bot: deployment long-context:x1-stable -> route updated for tenant acme (no restart needed).
ACME Ops: Pin worked — p95 dropped back to expected range ~220ms. Thanks.
Li (SRE): Good to confirm. We'll keep the pinned variant as a policy for you until we push a fix. @Tony can you share repro cases so we can hit CI with the exact unicode patterns?
Tony (Eng Runtime): Will collect and add unit tests. The fallback path appears to be caused by sequence framing with repeated U+FFFD replacement bytes from the customer's data ingestion pipeline; that confuses the multibyte scanner and triggers the slow path.
Sara (ML Ops): Proposed medium-term fix: make the fast tokenizer accept the malformed sequence or bail earlier with a graceful replacement token instead of invoking the python fallback. Also add a streaming tokenizer mode so long requests can be tokenized in chunks rather than all-at-once.
Maya (Support): ETA on medium-term? ACME would like timeline so they can plan.
Tony (Eng Runtime): I'll scope: quick patch to avoid fallback (hotfix) — ~2 days dev + 1 day rollout. Streaming tokenizer is larger — ~2 sprints.
ACME Ops: Patch timeline sounds fine. Are there additional knobs we can set to reduce surface area while patch is in progress?
Li (SRE): You can also lower `max_tokens` for generation or set `prefill_kv_cache: true` in the client config to reduce repeated tokenization across retryable requests. Another trick: split the prompt into smaller chunks and call `append` style streaming if the client supports it — that avoids re-tokenizing the entire 12k on retries.
ACME Ops: We'll try splitting in the short term. Do we need to rotate keys or anything?
Maya (Support): No auth rotation needed — this is purely runtime. We'll monitor.
Tony (Eng Runtime): For visibility, I've opened an internal PR and linked the failing test harness. PR: https://git.redwood/eng/runtime/pulls/4231 — contains a reproducer and perf tests.
Sara (ML Ops): Added an alert to detect tokenizer fallback ratio >0.5 for any model in prod; that will page @eng-runtime.
Li (SRE): Also scheduled a canary rollout of the hotfix to 10% traffic tomorrow 04:00 UTC so we can validate without broader risk.
ACME Ops: Thanks everyone — will keep pinned to x1 until you confirm the patch. Appreciate the quick triage. :thumbsup:
Maya (Support): Copy that. I'll leave this thread open and update once the hotfix is live and we've validated for ACME.
Tony (Eng Runtime): One more note for debugging logs — if you can include the first 256 bytes of the original payload (redact sensitive data), it helps us identify the exact byte patterns causing the fallback.
ACME Ops: Will send a sanitized sample via the secure upload link you provided.
Maya (Support): Marking this as high priority. Follow-ups: hotfix PR review, canary rollout, and ACME validation.
ACME Ops: Received the hotfix build (staging). Running tests now.
ACME Ops: Staging looks good — tokenizer fallback is gone in our tests and p99 reduced significantly. Please advise when production rollout is scheduled.
Tony (Eng Runtime): Production canary starts 2026-03-16 04:00 UTC per Li. We'll post completion here.
Li (SRE): Canary completed and metrics look good. Rolling to 100% in 2 hours.
Maya (Support): ACME — we pushed the prod fix. Please unpin when you're ready and report if you see any regression.
ACME Ops: Unpinning now; all good in prod. p95/p99 stable. Thanks all. :party:
